- **The task — or a persistent agent's standing contract — rides the SYSTEM PROMPT, and every agent request is checked for it.** A `bob run` task, or a resident agent's role + duties, is appended to the session's system prompt as LITERAL text through the resource loader's `appendSystemPromptOverride` (never as an append-system-prompt *source*: pi reads a source string that names an existing path as that FILE), built from WELL-FORMED text — unpaired surrogates removed the way pi-ai's adapters remove them from a request, so the adapters' own sanitizing is a no-op on the block and an equivalent request is not refused — bounded by a cap the block's own heading states and cut with a visible `[truncated: N chars elided]` marker: the block and its cap survive a compaction, and a task longer than the cap keeps only what fit under it — the elided tail does not come back. pi rebuilds the system prompt when it creates the session, on every reload and whenever the active tool set changes (a bind rebuilds only through one of those), reading the same loader append text each time — so the block is identical across rebuilds — while a context compaction rewrites only the message history. bob's guard is registered LAST on `before_provider_request`, after every declared capability. It does NOT parse provider payload shapes (the round-2 defect: a legitimate request under the Responses APIs' `input` or Google's `config.systemInstruction` layout failed) and it does not search a serialization (the round-3 defect: a body that wrote a character escaped, and pi-ai's OpenAI Completions adapter sanitizing the system prompt, each false-failed a legitimate request): it asks whether a DECODED string value in the payload carries the block, and an agent request that does not carry it fails the turn exactly like a failed audit — the session is disposed, the process ends, and the reason (`contract_missing_from_request`) is named. **What the guard proves is that every agent request carries the contract block** — the system prompt is where bob PUTS it, and the guard proves it is still SENT (a capability that moves the block into the conversation still passes). That covers both loss paths a capability has (replacing the prompt in `before_agent_start`, or rewriting the outgoing payload in `before_provider_request`), neither of which the creation/bind/reload audit can see. A blank task is refused BEFORE the session starts. There is NO exemption: pi's own compaction and branch-summary calls never reach the guard at all (pi attaches the hook to the agent's own requests, and the live test pins it), and a session-flag exemption would mis-fire — pi's `isCompacting` is also true during branch summarization, where a capability can start an agent turn. (`test/shell/system-prompt-contract.test.ts`, `system-prompt-contract-live.test.ts`, `run.test.ts`)
